REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTANT’S QUALIFICATIONS BASED SELECTION (CQS)

Name of Project

“Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People” (INSON)

Loan No/Credit No/ Grant Number

Credit 7555-UZ / Grant Agreement No. TF C4589-UZ

Assignment Title

Development of Continuous Professional Development Programs, a Sustainable Supervision System, and Methodological Support for Monitoring and Evaluation of a Priority Evidence-Based Social Intervention

Procurement Plan Ref Number

UZ-INSON-CS-CQS-1.1.5.1

Country of Delivery

Republic of Uzbekistan

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the INSON Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) include the development of a sustainable continuing professional development (CPD) system and modular professional development programs for social workers and other NASP/INSON staff; the development of a sustainable professional supervision system and methodological support for its initial pilot implementation; and methodological support for the monitoring, quality assessment, and further improvement of a priority evidence-based social intervention selected by the Client.

The scope of services includes the preparation and validation of at least six modular professional development programs and related training materials; a limited Training of Trainers (ToT) for 35-40 trainers from 14 regions; development of a professional supervision model, standards, tools, training package and support to a limited supervision pilot; a brief review of evidence-based social interventions and development and testing of monitoring and quality-assessment tools for one priority intervention; as well as knowledge transfer, quality assurance, and recommendations for institutionalization and sustainability.

The duration of the assignment is expected to be twelve (12) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR), including the full scope of services and qualification requirements, can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UBUEjGW-5VAVsiq4cnxi5H8ooq_PSr7K/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104755491226149341341&rtpof=true&sd=true

The National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan now invites eligible consulting organizations (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023) (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The best qualified Consultant will be selected in accordance with the CQS method set out in the Regulations, based on the qualification requirements set out in the TOR and summarized below.

Interested Consultants should meet the following qualification requirements:

  • Legally registered consulting company, university, research institution, or nonprofit organization eligible to enter into contracts in accordance with the applicable procurement rules;
  • At least ten (10) years of institutional experience in social work, social protection, capacity development, social services, or related fields;
  • Demonstrated experience in at least three (3) assignments of comparable complexity related to curriculum development, professional training systems, supervision, quality assurance, or evidence-based social interventions, collectively covering at least two of the above areas;
  • Demonstrated experience in providing technical assistance and adapting methodologies to different institutional and cultural contexts;
  • Experience working with government institutions and development partners;
  • Availability of sufficient technical, managerial, and administrative staff capacity to perform the assignment, together with internal quality assurance procedures.

Further information can be obtained through piuinsonprocurement@gmail.com during office hours from 09:00 to 17:00 Tashkent time.

Expressions of interest demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience must be delivered electronically to piuinsonprocurement@gmail.com by 17 September, 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Republic of Tajikistan

Sustainable Financing for Rogun Hydropower Project (P181029)

Projects Management Group for Energy Facilities Construction under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan (PMG EFC)

Grant No.: IDA-E3800

Assignment Title: Provision of International Advisory and Technical Support Services to the Project Management Group under the President of Tajikistan

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TJ-PMG-EFC-CS-QCBS-07

The Republic of Tajikistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Financing for Rogun Hydropower Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Provision of International Advisory and Technical Support Services to the Project Management Group under the President of Tajikistan (PMG).

The overall objective of this assignment is to provide Project Implementing Agency with high-level technical, managerial, procurement, contract management, civil works, electromechanical, and environmental & social expertise required for effective oversight of the Rogun HPP project during the construction phase, including for the oversight of the Project Management Consultant (PMC), the HSE Supervisor, the Dam Safety Panel of Experts (DSPoE) and the Environmental and Social Panel of Experts (ESPoE) and Contractors.

The scope of services includes, among others, the following:

  1. Supporting Project Implementing Agency in the overall technical, managerial, procurement, contractual, and environmental and social oversight of the Project;
  2. Reviewing reports, deliverables, recommendations, and decisions prepared by the Project Management Consultant and other consultants;
  3. Advising Project Implementing Agency on technical, contractual, procurement, and E&S matters related to the Project;
  4. Participating in coordination meetings with the Project Management Consultant, contractors, financiers, and other stakeholders, as required by Project Implementing Agency;
  5. Supporting Project Implementing Agency in decision-making processes by providing independent professional opinions;
  6. Contributing to capacity strengthening of Project Implementing Agency through on-the-job support and knowledge transfer.

Anticipated date for commencement of the Services is April 2027 and the tentative duration of the assignment for the Services is 3 years.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the link 

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aSBkt_BCeH9RthhpzxaFJUq6TdS0b7yK/view?usp=sharing 

but can be obtained at the address given at the end of this REoI.

The Project Management Group for Energy Facilities Construction under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan (PMG) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Legal status. The Consultant shall be a legally registered entity that has been established and operating for at least the last ten (10) years. A copy of the certificate of incorporation or an equivalent registration document issued by the relevant authority in the country of establishment shall be provided. In the case of a joint venture (JV), this requirement shall apply to each JV member.
  2. General experience. The Consultant shall have at least fifteen (15) years of experience in providing advisory, owner’s-engineer, project-management, construction-supervision, or technical-support services to project implementing agencies or employers responsible for large dam and hydropower projects.
  3. Specific experience.

The Consultant shall demonstrate the following experience on large dam or hydropower projects:

  1. technical-support and/or owner’s-engineer services;
  2. construction-supervision services;
  3. contract-administration support under FIDIC-based contracts, including claims and variations management; and
  4. services in i, ii, or iii above on a project financed by the World Bank, AIIB, ADB, EIB, or another Multilateral Development Bank.

The above experience may be demonstrated through one or more assignments. However, the Consultant shall demonstrate at least one (1) principal assignment for a large dam or hydropower project with an installed capacity of at least 300 MW and a dam height of at least 100 m. The underlying construction-works value of the principal referenced project shall be at least US$300 million.

For each referenced assignment used to demonstrate any of the above requirements, the Consultant shall provide the name of the assignment, location and country, name of the client, description and scope of the services performed, Consultant’s contract value, value of the underlying construction works, duration, years of execution, completion status, and the Consultant’s role in the assignment.

In the case of a JV, the experience of the JV members may be combined. However, the experience of proposed subconsultants, affiliated entities, or individual experts shall not be considered the corporate experience of the Consultant or the JV members.

4. Capacity to deliver. The Consultant shall submit a detailed organogram demonstrating the managerial and organizational capability to carry out the assignment, and shall provide evidence of a quality management system (ISO 9001 or equivalent).

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (Seventh Edition, September 2025) (Procurement Regulations) setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly in the Expression of Interest whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 17:00.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form in English to the address below (in person, or by mail) September 16, 2026, by 14:00 pm, Dushanbe time.

Request for Expression of Interest (Consulting Services - Competitive Selection of a Firm Based on Qualifications)

Kyrgyz Republic 

Enhancing Resilience in Kyrgyzstan Project (ERIK, ERIK AF)

Loan No. IDA 66870 Grant No. IDA D6550

Tender No. KG-CS/CQS-09

Assignment Title: Consulting services «Enhancing Claims Management for the Mandatory Insurance of Residential Buildings Against Emergency Situations in Kyrgyzstan»

Component 3 of the project «Enhancing Resilience in Kyrgyzstan (ERIK)»: Enhancing Financial Protection and Insurance Against Natural Disaster Risks.

Responsible agencies: the Financial Market Regulation and Supervision Service under the Ministry of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic and State Insurance Organization OJSC.

The main objective of the Component is to support the efforts of the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic in reducing the financial impacts of emergencies.

To support the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic, the State Insurance Organization (SIO), and any future potential collective insurance pool to strengthen the institutional and operational foundations of claims management for the mandatory residential insurance in Kyrgyzstan.

Specifically, the assignment aims to:

•Analyze the current state and prepare proposals for modernizing claims management procedures to increase the efficiency of claim administration and loss assessment methodology, including development of internal regulations for claim settlement;

•Planning surge capacity to manage a high volume of claims following major disaster events;

•Reviewing OJSC “SIO” existing IT system and developing recommendations for the structure of claims processing for mandatory residential building insurance through OJSC “SIO” IT system;

•Deliver capacity-building to Gosfinnadzor, OJSC “SIO” and other relevant stakeholders on the proposed changes to the procedures and on the use of disaster relief bonds.

The consultant will deliver technical and advisory services on enhancing claims management for the mandatory insurance of residential buildings against Emergency Situations in Kyrgyzstan.

The start of the assignment is scheduled for October 2026. The expected duration of the assignment is approximately 6 months after the contract is signed with the selected Consultant and 12 months of advisory support after completion of the main contract.

The estimated budget for the assignment, including all taxes (including local taxes), should not exceed $250,000.00 USD.

Name of Project: Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People (INSON) Project

Contract Title: Procurement of Specialized Equipment for Social Service and Rehabilitation Institutions

Credit No.: 7555-UZ / Grant No.: TF C4589-UZ

RFB Reference No.: UZ-INSON-RFB-2.2.7-8

 

  1. The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People (INSON) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contracts for Procurement of Specialized Equipment for Social Service and Rehabilitation Institutions. For these contracts, the Borrower may process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing, except for those payments, which the contract provides to be made through letter of credit.

2.         The National Agency for Social Protection under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan (NASP) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Specialized Equipment for Social Service and Rehabilitation Institutions, as follows:

  • Lot 01: Pediatric/adult rehab trainers and robotics (mechanotherapy).

Lot 01 comprises pediatric and adult rehabilitation trainers and robotic mechanotherapy systems for gait, balance, and limb function restoration. It includes advanced gait and balance training systems, robotic and mechanized upper- and lower-limb trainers. The lot also contains pediatric and adult gait imitation devices, bodyweight supported walking systems, and various mechanotherapy frames and wallmounted units. Additional balance, step, ramp, and platform accessories support progressive and taskoriented training across different functional levels. There are about 50 line items (systems), the quantities per item typically vary from 20 to 55 sets but may be lower or higher, up to 110-140 sets for some items.

  • Lot 02: Pediatric/adult mobility aids and seating

Lot 2 comprises pediatric and adult mobility aids and seating systems, including wheelchairs, specialized strollers, walkers, and adaptive seating for different age and size groups. It covers indoor and outdoor mobility devices, heightadjustable and tiltinspace chairs, and rehabilitation strollers designed to support posture, pressure distribution, and safe transportation. The lot also includes supportive seating for therapy and daily activities. There are 10 line items, including the total of 550 walking devices of various sizes, 550 baby wheelchairs of various sizes, 110 chairs for children with cerebral palsy, 40 multifunctional adaptive chairs, and 55 safe adaptive chairs for children with disabilities.

  • Lot 03: Small rehab tools, hand therapy and occupational therapy accessories

Lot 03 comprises small rehabilitation tools, handtherapy devices and occupational therapy accessories, with over than 30 line items in total. It includes freeweight sets and small exercise equipment for strengthening and rangeofmotion training, portable handtherapy tools (e.g. grip and finger trainers, elastic resistance bands and bars), and compact jointmobilization and stretching devices for upper and lower limbs. The lot also covers assorted small OT accessories to support finemotor training, coordination, and basic activities of daily living. The total quantities per line item range from 55 to 550 units to equip all participating institutions.

  • Lot 04: Sensory integration, play structures, mats and flooring

Lot 04 comprises sensory integration equipment, play structures, mats and flooring, about 20 line items in total. It includes modular sensory integration frames, swings and suspension systems, tactile and balance paths, and soft play elements that support vestibular, proprioceptive and tactile stimulation. The lot also provides protective floor and wall mats, crash mats, and foam blocks for safe movement, as well as small goaloriented play sets to structure therapeutic activities in pediatric and adult sensory rooms, with total quantities per line item typically ranging from 55 to 110 units to equip all facilities.

  • Lot 05: Pediatric/adult therapy furniture, support frames and positioning aids

Lot 05 comprises pediatric and adult therapy furniture, support frames and positioning aids, there are about 15 line items in total. It includes heightadjustable therapy tables and desks, adaptive therapy chairs, and specialized seating systems that provide postural support during rehabilitation and daily activities. The lot also covers standing frames and support frames for safe upright positioning, as well as complex adjustable positioning systems (including multimodule seating/standing solutions) for children and adults with significant motor impairments, with total quantities per line item typically ranging from 35 to 55 sets to equip all facilities.

  • Lot 06: Electrophysical therapy equipment (physiotherapy).

Lot 06 comprises electrophysical therapy equipment for physiotherapy, with 06 line items in total. It includes a professional thermotherapy system (20 sets), apparatus for galvanization and medical electrophoresis (20 sets), extracorporeal shockwave therapy device (20 sets), combined multi-channel modular physiotherapy device (55 sets), lymphatic drainage therapy device (55 sets), and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS/rTMS) system (5 sets), together covering the main electrophysical modalities needed for pain management, edema reduction, and tissue healing in adult and pediatric patients.

  • Lot 07: Ophthalmological equipment.

Lot 07 comprises ophthalmic diagnostic equipment for regional MSEC offices, enabling comprehensive eye examination capabilities. The package includes seven equipment categories: slit lamps with digital imaging systems, stationary and portable autorefractor-keratometers for automated refraction measurement, portable fundus cameras for retinal imaging, trial lens sets for subjective refraction testing, LED visual acuity projectors, and specialized diagnostic lenses for posterior segment examination. The quantities vary from 14 to 15 sets per item.

  • Lot 08: Diagnostic and rehabilitation equipment.

Lot 08 covers advanced neurorehabilitation therapy equipment, including standalone interactive systems for balance assessment/training (12 sets), isokinetic muscle performance evaluation and training systems (6 sets), and hand/upperlimb rehabilitation training systems (12 sets).

            Required delivery period should not exceed 16 weeks. Following arrival to Uzbekistan the supplier shall deliver the goods to 55 Territorial Social Service Centers (TSSCs), 12 Rehabilitation Centers and 14 Medical-Social Expert Commissions (MSECs) located throughout the country, assemble, install and commission the goods, as further defined in the technical specifications, and provide training to end-user personnel on operation of the goods supplied. The margin of preference for goods manufactured in Uzbekistan shall not apply.

3.         Bidders may Bid for one or several contracts (lots), as further defined in the Bidding document.

4.         Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016, revised September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

5.         Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents.

The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors):

  • Lots 01, 02, 05, 06, 07, 08: 30% (thirty percent)
  • Lots 03, 04: 20% (twenty percent)

The following weightings shall apply for Bid cost (price factors):

  • Lots 01, 02, 05, 06, 07, 08: 70% (seventy percent)
  • Lots 03, 04: 80% (eighty percent)

6.         Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the INSON Project Implementation Unit (INSON PIU), Attn.: Mr. Mirodil Khusanov, INSON Project Coordinator, and Mr. Sardor Makhmudov, Procurement Specialist, e-mail: piuinsonprocurement@gmail.com (cc: m.xusanov@ihma.uz, s.maxmudov@ihma.uz)  and inspect the bidding document during the office hours, i.e. 10:00 to 17:00 hours local at the address given below.

Alternatively, the Bidding Document may be downloaded at the following weblink: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1iXUdRzeu7bJs15V7HNTemf5EuJml_DeM?usp=sharing. In the latter case, the Bidder shall submit a written application after downloading the Bidding Document, and shall have registered with the Purchaser for the purposes of subsequent notification (e.g. in case of clarifications or addenda issued pursuant to ITB 7 or ITB 8). A Bidder who has not registered with the Purchaser as required above, shall bear sole responsibility for monitoring and obtaining clarifications or addenda which may be made available at the above link or published at the Purchaser's webpage specified in ITB 7.1.

8.         Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 11:00 a.m. Tashkent local time (UTC+05:00) on 9 October 2026. Electronic Bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. records.description:
Specific Procurement Notice

 

Request for Bids

Plant
Design, Supply and Installation

(Two-envelope Bidding Process, Without Prequalification)

 

Employer:

JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan

Project:

Electricity Sector Transformation and Resilient Transmission (ESTART)

Contract title:

Modernization and upgrade of main grid substations: Gulcha SS 220 kV, 0 SS 220 kV, Gornaya SS 220 kV Daugiz-Tau SS 220 kV.

Country:

Republic of Uzbekistan

Credit/Loan No.:

IDA-69430, TF0B5804-UZ

RFB No:

RFB/MUTS/2021-7R

Issued on:

July 13, 2026

 

1.         The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Electricity Sector Transformation and Resilient Transmission (ESTART) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the Contract for Modernization and upgrade of main grid substations: Gulcha SS 220 kV, 0 SS 220 kV, Gornaya SS 220 kV Daugiz-Tau SS 220 kV. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing, except for those payments, which the contract provides to be made through letter of credit.

2.        The JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan (NEGU) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Modernization and upgrade of main grid substations: Gulcha SS 220 kV, 0 SS 220 kV, Gornaya SS 220 kV Daugiz-Tau SS 220 kV.

The Bidders’ qualification requirements include:

The qualification requirements for bidders, including General Experience, Specific Experience, Financial Capabilities, and other requirements set out in Section III of the RFB, shall apply. In the event of any discrepancy between the requirements stated herein and those specified in Section III of the RFB, the provisions of Section III shall prevail.

General Experience:

Experience in Energy sector under contracts in the role of contractor, subcontractor or management contractor for at least the last ten (10) years starting 1st January 2016.

Specific Experience:

Participation as a contractor, joint venture member[1], management contractor, or subcontractor, in at least two (2) contracts each with a value of at least USD 22,400,000.00 (Twenty-two million and four hundred thousand United States Dollars) or one (1) contract with a value of at least USD 42,000,000.00 (Forty-two million United States dollars) within the last ten (10) years (2016-2025), that have been successfully and substantially[2] completed and that are similar to the proposed Plant and Installation Services. The similarity of the contracts shall be based on Design, supply, installation, modernization/rehabilitation testing, and commissioning of 220 kV or above substation.

For the above or other contracts executed within the last ten (10) years, a minimum experience in the following key activities:

  1. Preparation of detailed engineering design for the modernization of at least two (2) 220 kV (or above) substation.
  2. Supply and installation of major Plant and Equipment: Autotransformer, instrument transformers, relay protection, and automation devices, circuit breaker, and disconnectors for 220 kV (or above) Substation.
  3. Supply and installation of at least two (2) transformer units rated at a minimum 220 kV and not less than 200 MVA each.  
  4. Design, Installation, and Commissioning of relay protection devices and secondary equipment & control cabinets for 220 kV (or above) substation for at least two (2) substations.
  5. Design, Installation, and Commissioning for HF equipment and Emergency automation (220 kV and above) substations for at least two (2) substations.

Financial Capabilities:

Submission of audited balance sheets or if not required by the law of the Bidder’s Country, other financial statements acceptable to the Employer, for the last five years 2021-2025 to demonstrate the current soundness of the Bidders financial position and its prospective long-term profitability.

Minimum average annual turnover of USD 28,000,000.00 (twenty-eight million United States Dollars), calculated as total certified payments received for contracts in progress and/or completed within past three years (2023-2025), divided by three.

Access to, or availability of, financial resources such as liquid assets, unencumbered real assets, lines of credit, and other financial means, other than any contractual advance payments to meet: (i) the following cash-flow requirement: USD 5,600,000.00 (Five million six hundred thousand United States Dollars) and (ii) the overall cash flow requirements for this contract and its current commitments.

Experience in managing ES aspects

Experience as prime contractor, joint venture member, or Subcontractor between 1st January 2021 and Application submission deadline, in managing ES risks and impacts in the following aspects:

1.   Assessment and Management of Environmental and Social Risks and Impacts.

2.   Labour and working Condition.

3.        Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4.        Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan, Ismoiljon Abduganiev – PIU Manager (pmu.modernization@gmail.com) and inspect the Bidding document during office hours 09:00 to 17:00 hours at the address given below.

5.        Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): [50%] and for Bid cost: [50%].

6.        The bidding document in English may be obtained by interested bidders on the submission of an application for bidding documents by sending a request to the email address: pmu.modernization@gmail.com.The document will be sent by e-mail to the address indicated in the application.

7.        Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before September 4, 2026 at 11:00 Tashkent time. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. The outer Bid envelopes marked “ORIGINAL BID”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on September 4, 2026 at 11:00 Tashkent time. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in the safe custody of the Employer until the second public Bid opening.

8.        All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security of USD 280,000.00 (Two hundred and eighty thousand United States Dollars).

9.        Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.

10.      The address referred to above is:

JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan

Osiyo street 42, Yunusobod district, Tashkent 100084, Uzbekistan.

Floor 4, Room 401.

Phone: +99871 236 66 28.  e-mail: pmu.modernization@gmail.com

 

[1]    For contracts under which the Bidder participated as a joint venture member or sub-contractor, only the Bidder’s share, by value, shall be considered to meet this requirement

[2]     Substantial completion shall be based on 80% or more Plant and installation completed under the contract.
